blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Air quality at Ateneo de Zamboanga University remained hazardous on Wednesday, with pollution levels falling from “emergency” to “very unhealthy.” The Department of Environment and Natural Resources – Environmental Management Bureau (DENR-EMB) reported the change in its 5 p.m. advisory on Wednesday, Oct. 14. The agency said the particulate matter (PM) 2.5 concentration at its Ateneo de Zamboanga University Tumaga station in Zamboanga City registered an air quality index (AQI) of 151 to 200, or “very unhealthy” levels. PM2.5 refers to fine particulate matter measuring 2.5 micrometers or less in diameter. The area reached emergency levels at noon […]...
